AI Cybersecurity  ·  Managed Detection & Response Everyone promises detection. Ask for the number.

Every provider promises detection. Few will put in writing how long the last missed attack went unseen. We run the service around the clock, measure that time per entry path and report it to you every quarter.

24/7 · ANNUAL TERMMEASURED DWELL TIMEEFFECTIVENESS TESTED INDEPENDENTLY
The decisions underneath

Three questions decide the service.

Detection services are compared on tooling and staffing. They should be compared on where the coverage sits and how fast it is proven.

01

At which stage would you have seen it

Coverage at entry and coverage at objective are very different services. Dwell time, meaning how long an attacker goes unnoticed, is decided in the stages in between.

02

What is the measured number

Not the target and not the SLA (service-level agreement). The number actually achieved, including the case that went badly.

03

Who tests whether it works

A test run by the operator’s own team carries little weight, however rigorous it is. The tester should sit outside the team that runs the service.

How the path runs

Detection is a placement problem.

Every one of these paths is detectable. The question a service has to answer is at which stage, and how quickly. Choose an entry point.

ENTRY

FOOTHOLD

ATTACK PATH— GATES USUALLY PRESENT
Select an entry point

Five stages, from the way in to the thing the attacker came for. What changes between paths is how long each stage stays invisible.

We measure dwell time per entry path and report it to you every quarter. That includes the paths where we were slow to see something.

The boundary

We run it around the clock. Someone independent tests it.

Three steps. We operate the service and close the gaps. The test in the middle belongs to a party outside our operations team.

STEP 01 · ORVIX

We operate the service

Detection engineering, triage, response and the reporting that goes with it, 24/7 under an annual term. Escalation rules are agreed in writing before the service goes live.

STEP 02 · INDEPENDENT TESTER

An independent party tests it

Effectiveness testing is done by a party that does not report to the team running the service. When the result must carry weight with a board or regulator, that party is fully independent of Orvix.

STEP 03 · ORVIX

We close what the test found

Every detection gap the test finds becomes engineering work with a date. The tester runs the re-test.

Keeping the operator and the tester apart is the standard we ask of every supplier. We apply it to our own service first.

Questions we are asked

Before you ask us.

Do you replace our SOC (security operations center) or work with it?
Either. Where an internal team exists the more common arrangement is that we hold the hours and the depth they cannot, and the escalation boundary is written down before the first incident rather than negotiated during one.
What dwell time do you commit to?
We measure dwell time per entry path and report it to you every quarter. A single figure averaged across every way in would hide exactly the paths you should be asking about.
Who performs the effectiveness testing?
A party that does not report to the team operating the service. When the result needs to carry weight with a board or regulator, that party is fully independent of Orvix, which is what makes the result credible.
Can you operate in Saudi Arabia?
Yes. Managed security operations in the Kingdom are licensed, so the service runs through a licensed partner under its own license, named in the contract.

Start with the last thing you missed.

Thirty minutes. Bring the incident that took longest to notice and we will map where a gate could have sat.
